Schedule of vector control campaigns

Source: R/xml_export.R
om_campaigns.Rd

Builds the schedule of deploy_OM_vector_control and get_OM_xml (which keep it for om_scenario_values): one row per campaign, with its date and coverage, from regular dates (from, to, every) or given dates.

Usage

om_campaigns(
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  every = "1 year",
  coverage,
  by_year = FALSE,
  dates = NULL,
  end_date = NULL
)

Arguments

from, to

First and last possible dates ("YYYY-MM-DD"); the campaigns are seq(from, to, by = every).

every

Interval between campaigns, as by in seq.Date: "1 year" (default), "6 months", "3 weeks", ...

coverage

Coverage: a number in [0, 1] or a placeholder (e.g. "@contITNcov@"), used for every campaign, or one value per campaign.

by_year

Logical (default FALSE): with a placeholder coverage, one placeholder per year ("@histITNcov@" becomes "@histITNcov2015@", "@histITNcov2016@", ...), as byyear of openMalariaUtilities' deploy_it_compat().

dates

Dates of the campaigns, instead of from, to and every.

end_date

Optional end of the simulated period ("YYYY-MM-DD", after the last campaign): the dummy hosts of dummy-host interventions last until then (otherwise 100 years). Kept with the schedule, so that deploy_OM_vector_control() and get_OM_xml() need no end_date argument.

Value

Data frame with date and coverage, and the end_date as an attribute when given (subsetting the data frame drops it).

Examples

# Annual campaigns, one coverage placeholder per year
om_campaigns("2015-01-25", "2018-01-25", coverage = "@histITNcov@", by_year = TRUE)
#>         date         coverage
#> 1 2015-01-25 @histITNcov2015@
#> 2 2016-01-25 @histITNcov2016@
#> 3 2017-01-25 @histITNcov2017@
#> 4 2018-01-25 @histITNcov2018@
# Same coverage every year, period ending in 2031
om_campaigns("2019-01-25", "2030-01-25", coverage = "@contITNcov@",
             end_date = "2031-01-01")
#>          date     coverage
#> 1  2019-01-25 @contITNcov@
#> 2  2020-01-25 @contITNcov@
#> 3  2021-01-25 @contITNcov@
#> 4  2022-01-25 @contITNcov@
#> 5  2023-01-25 @contITNcov@
#> 6  2024-01-25 @contITNcov@
#> 7  2025-01-25 @contITNcov@
#> 8  2026-01-25 @contITNcov@
#> 9  2027-01-25 @contITNcov@
#> 10 2028-01-25 @contITNcov@
#> 11 2029-01-25 @contITNcov@
#> 12 2030-01-25 @contITNcov@
# Given dates and coverages
om_campaigns(dates = c("2021-01-01", "2024-01-01"), coverage = c(0.8, 0.6))
#>         date coverage
#> 1 2021-01-01      0.8
#> 2 2024-01-01      0.6
